**Vejle: Børne- Og Ungdomspsykiatrisk Ambulatorium** (also referred to as PSY Børne- Og Ungdomspsykiatrisk Ambulatorium (Vejle)) is a child and adolescent psychiatric department operating within [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] in Denmark. It is frequently evaluated in the national ADHD database's annual quality reports, which monitor diagnostic practices, resource allocation, and adherence to clinical guidelines across the country's psychiatric facilities.

The department is particularly notable for its exceptional performance regarding [[indikator-2a|Indikator 2a]], a quality metric that measures the proportion of ADHD assessments for children aged 0–5 who receive a clinical environmental observation within 120 days of the assessment's start. In the 2023/24 reporting period, Vejle achieved a 100% fulfillment rate (14 out of 14 cases) for this standard [^src1]. It was one of only two departments in the country, alongside [[aabenna-borne-og-ungdomspsykiatrisk-ambulatorium|Aabenraa: Børne og Ungdomspsykiatrisk Ambulatorium]], to successfully reach the 100% development target for this specific indicator [^src2]. The department has also consistently met this standard in previous years.

However, the clinic's performance is mixed when looking at other diagnostic metrics and age groups. For [[indicator-2b|indicator-2b]], which tracks structured diagnostic interviews or environmental observations for children and adolescents aged 6–17, Vejle recorded a 58% fulfillment rate (95% CI: 53–63) in 2023/24 [^src3]. Furthermore, the department struggles significantly with [[indikator-3|Indikator 3]], which relates to diagnostic conferences. Among departments handling more than three cases, Vejle recorded the lowest performance in the dataset, with fulfillment dropping to just 8% [^src4]. 

In broader regional evaluations, Vejle, along with Esbjerg, is noted as contributing to a regional decline in target fulfillment for indicator 1. Ultimately, Vejle's profile in the national database illustrates the complex, systemic variations in Danish ADHD diagnostics, where a facility may excel in early childhood observational assessments while facing severe bottlenecks or compliance issues in multidisciplinary conferences and older age cohorts.
